name: Greater Somalia
summary: Greater Somalia (pan-Somalism) holds that the Somali people, divided by European and Ethiopian partition among Somalia, Djibouti, Ethiopia's Ogaden and Kenya's Northern Frontier District, should be reunited in one state. In its independence-era form it was a parliamentary, Muslim-majority nationalism that pursued unification officially by legal and peaceful means while backing armed kin and building a large army, and it takes no distinctive stance on the economy.
scope: The mainstream pan-Somali nationalism of the independence era (Somali Youth League, the 1960 Somali Republic constitution, the five-pointed star flag, the 1960s claims on Ogaden and the NFD), with its post-1969 and Barre-era armed form noted but not treated as the core. It excludes Barre's scientific socialism as such, the Islamist (al-Shabaab) appropriation of the idea, and Somaliland or Puntland separatism. Many economic and social answers are therefore low-confidence inferences from the constitution's Islamic and welfare provisions.

sources.usedFor: Article on promoting union of Somali territories by legal and peaceful means, Islam as state religion and main source of law, popular sovereignty, rights, property, welfare and the parliamentary system.

sources.title: Somalia: Siad Barre and Scientific Socialism (Country Study, Library of Congress)
sources.author: Library of Congress
sources.usedFor: The later Barre-era ideology, shallow Marxism, one-party rule and personality cult, used to mark the strand excluded from the core.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 1960 constitution has the state protect public health and promote free medical assistance for the indigent, a partial commitment short of fully universal care.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The constitution only requires equal pay for equal work; pan-Somalism has no wage doctrine and an overwhelmingly pastoral economy had little wage labour.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The movement is defined by territory, not economics; the independence-era economy was a mix of livestock trade and aid-funded state projects, so adherents were split.

public-ownership.rationale: Pan-Somalism took no stand; the 1960s republic was mixed while the later Barre state nationalised industry, so answers split by period.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No source ties the cause to tax policy and the economy had few very wealthy people; no basis to lean either way.

unions-good.rationale: The 1960 constitution protects labour but unions were marginal in a pastoral society, and the cause is not about labour.

property-fundamental.rationale: The constitution guarantees property but allows expropriation for public interest with compensation, a middle position not specific to the cause.

regulate-corporations.rationale: There were almost no corporations and the cause never addressed them; nothing to infer from its core aims.

cut-welfare.rationale: A poor post-colonial state with a constitutional commitment to social protection would not favour cutting welfare, though this is inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; the nationalist cause is class-neutral and stresses clan and national solidarity over worker control.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed by pan-Somalists; security-state behaviour appears only in the Barre regime, which is a later strand.

legalize-drugs.rationale: A conservative Muslim society where Islam is the main source of law would not legalise recreational drugs; inferred from the Islamic framework.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The question is not addressed; the constitution protects expression generally and the cause cites ethnic grievance, not speech law.

strong-leader.rationale: Independence-era pan-Somalism worked through parliamentary parties such as the SYL, and the constitution bars any individual from claiming sovereignty.

state-harmful.rationale: Adherents aim to build a larger Somali state; the constitution vests sovereignty in the people and the state is the vehicle of unification.

limit-guns.rationale: Armed pastoral clans and guerrilla support (shifta, WSLF) were part of the struggle, so strict gun limits are unlikely; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Somalia built a large military after independence largely to back its claims, and politicians who seemed soft risked falling.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Islam is the state religion and main source of law, so legal sex work is rejected.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not a pan-Somali topic; Islamic law and customary justice both favour retribution and compensation alongside reform.

traditional-family.rationale: The republic rested on Islamic personal status law and customary kinship society, so traditional family is a baseline value.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: With Islam as the state religion and its law the main source of law, same-sex marriage is rejected.

abortion-legal.rationale: Islamic legal framework and conservative society restrict abortion; inferred rather than stated.

more-religion-public.rationale: Islam is the state religion and the main source of law, but pan-Somalism is ethnic rather than religious, so religion's role is secondary.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The cause targets colonial partition rather than racial redress policies; not addressed.

gender-social-construct.rationale: A traditional Muslim society would hold gender as largely given; inferred from the Islamic framework.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Shared language, culture and pastoral tradition are the basis of the claim that Somalis are one nation, so preserving them is central.

gradual-change.rationale: The goal demanded revising colonial borders, so adherents wanted change to the established order, though through legal means in the 1960 formula.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration was not an issue; the cause welcomes ethnic Somalis from neighbouring states as citizens, which cuts against restricting them.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The constitution accepts sovereignty limits for peace and Somalia took its claims to the UN and OAU, though it resented their refusal to revise borders.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; Somalia was a small exporter of livestock and bananas, with no stated trade doctrine in the cause.

nation-first.rationale: Constitution accepts cooperation and solidarity, while the irredentist claim openly put the Somali nation ahead of OAU border norms; adherents split.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; the constitution repudiates war for settling disputes, but Somalia backed armed kin in neighbouring states.

open-borders.rationale: Pan-Somalism wants the borders redrawn to enclose Somalis, not abolished, though Somalis would move freely within the unified state.

limit-growth.rationale: A poor, aid-dependent country seeking development; no environmental ideology; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed by the movement, which long predates climate politics.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The cause has no view on technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed at all; no basis in the movement's aims.

revolution-justified.rationale: The legal-peaceful formula was paired with guerrilla support such as the shifta and WSLF, and later revolutionary regimes, so adherents accept armed struggle.

experts-over-public.rationale: The constitution rests sovereignty on the people and clan elders and assemblies carried authority, so experts are not preferred.

central-planning.rationale: Only the Barre period used planning under scientific socialism; independence-era adherents had no such view, so split.

socialized-markets.rationale: Barre's version mixed socialism and Islam, the earlier republic did not; no shared position.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; no relevance to pastoral clan land use.

basic-income.rationale: A poor state could not afford it and the cause has no welfare doctrine; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed; Somalia had almost no industry to protect.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State-led development was mainstream in post-colonial states and under Barre, but not a theme of the cause itself.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Constitution protects property in general terms; pastoral clan land tenure had no clear fit with the statement.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The constitution guarantees property and paid labour with equal pay, and no Somali nationalist current sought to abolish them.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A new state building a currency and banks would keep them; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The pan-Somali cause has no view on state-recognised wage bodies, and the economy had almost no organised employers or unions.

one-party-rule.rationale: The independence-era mainstream was multiparty parliamentary democracy under the 1960 constitution; the one-party Barre system is a later strand.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The republic had a president and parliament, and Somali clans traditionally lacked kings; a monarch is not part of the cause.

democracy-best.rationale: The 1960 constitution is a parliamentary democracy based on popular sovereignty, which Somalis took pride in at independence.

direct-votes.rationale: The constitution was representative; direct votes were not discussed.

workers-councils.rationale: The constitution places power in an elected National Assembly, and the cause has no workers' council tradition.

right-to-secede.rationale: Pan-Somalism says Somalis in Ogaden and the NFD may choose to leave Ethiopia and Kenya under self-determination, though it rejects secession from Somalia.

natural-rulers.rationale: The 1960 constitution sets equal rights and duties for citizens, and Somali clan custom was egalitarian among men.

political-violence-never.rationale: Official policy was peaceful means, but the cause also supported shifta and WSLF insurgents and fought wars in 1964 and 1977.

war-builds-character.rationale: The constitution repudiates war as a means of settling disputes; adherents frame wars as defence of kin, not character building.

separate-church-state.rationale: Islam is the state religion and the main source of legislation under the constitution.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Islamic doctrine is the main source of law (art. 50) and Muslims' personal status follows sharia, though not the sole source.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The cause aims at a unified state with a national army and courts, as the constitution provides.

military-superiority.rationale: Somalia built armed forces larger than its neighbours' to back its claims, and adherents wanted strength against Ethiopia.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The core claim is that all ethnic Somalis belong in one state, and the constitution makes all ethnic Somalis citizens wherever they live.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The movement sees colonial partition and ethnic division as the driver, not class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed; constitution gives equal rights and duties but says nothing on equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Somalis see themselves as native to the Ogaden and NFD, supporting authority over traditional lands, but the statement is framed around minority indigenous peoples.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Adherents blame colonial and Ethiopian partition for lost territories, but no source shows a reparations demand.

civilizational-union.rationale: The constitution urges solidarity with African and Islamic peoples but not political union; unity is sought only among Somalis.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Clan and nation solidarity are central values; inferred, not stated.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The constitution lists equal rights and duties together, so neither is placed first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Neither the cause nor the 1960 constitution says anything on nature's intrinsic worth, so no stance can be inferred.

limit-population.rationale: A conservative Muslim pastoral society favoured large families; inferred from the Islamic framework.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; a poor country seeking modernisation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The movement's aims are territorial, and no source links it to speeding up technological disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; a conservative Islamic framework would be cautious, inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic for the independence-era cause; a mild lean against inferred from its clan-assembly politics.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in the cause.

restore-past-order.rationale: The cause appeals to a past of Somali unity before partition and the Dervish resistance, but also pursues modern statehood.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Pan-Somalism is a fixed national goal pursued regardless of cost, but no source states a view on judging policy by results.

direct-action.rationale: Official line was parliamentary and diplomatic, but armed groups and guerrillas carried part of the effort.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed; mixed conduct of peaceful law and force.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Somalis are mainly pastoralists seeking a modern state, and no wing wants hunter-gatherer life.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: No Somali nationalist source proposes this; a modern state needs specialists.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Barre's socialism used egalitarian language but the cause itself did not; split.

production-for-use.rationale: Only Barre-era scientific socialism leaned this way; not in the cause.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist ideas were shallow in Somalia and the cause is nationalist; inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Marxist sympathies were shallow and pan-Somalism is a cross-class national cause.

collective-farming.rationale: Barre promoted cooperatives but pastoral clans resisted; the cause itself did not call for it.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The cause blames colonial partition and Ethiopian expansion for conflict, not capitalism as such.

taxation-theft.rationale: The constitution requires citizens to contribute through taxes under law; no Somali current rejects taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: Islamic law sets moral limits beyond harm; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The cause is about rights of a people and clans, not just individuals, though the constitution also protects individual rights.

conscription.rationale: A state with a large military behind irredentist aims would draft; inferred, not stated.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The constitution makes the vote and popular sovereignty central.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed; the state is seen as embodying the nation, not as a firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: The constitution lists rights and welfare duties but no source frames freedom as requiring material means, so the answer is neutral.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; radio (Voice of Somalia) mattered but the statement is a Western frame.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; Somali nationalism defines nationhood by language, culture and kinship, not racial ranking.

organic-representation.rationale: Clan-based representation was informal reality in Somali politics, though parties competed in elections.

total-state.rationale: The constitution protects individual freedoms and limits the state; total state control belongs to no pan-Somali programme.

national-rebirth.rationale: The cause seeks unification of a divided people rather than decadence-and-rebirth rhetoric.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Somalia claimed self-determination for Somalis in Ogaden, NFD and Djibouti and fought over them, though officially not as sovereignty claims.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The constitution rests authority on popular sovereignty, though clan loyalty is a social fact.

bound-labor.rationale: The constitution prohibits forced and compulsory labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: A philosophical question outside the concerns of the Somali unification cause, with no source to draw on.

universal-morality.rationale: Islamic framework implies universal morals known through revelation, not strictly reason; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: The cause seeks one unified Somalia but gives no theory of a single reasoned common good versus competing interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; Somalia is an Islamic state expressing solidarity with Islamic peoples, so a Jewish state in Israel is likely opposed, inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The constitution made all ethnic Somalis citizens wherever they live, implying a right to belong to the homeland.

revive-national-language.rationale: Somali was a living language, not lapsed; the republic faced the question of choosing a written script, not reviving it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: With almost no large companies in Somalia, the cause never discussed democratic control of firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; schooling was minimal and state-run.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Somalia's budget was aid-dependent and the cause is not about fiscal policy, so no view can be inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: The cause links political freedom to national self-determination, not to economic freedom, and no source connects them.

rule-by-example.rationale: The constitution rests on law and an elected assembly.

national-self-determination.rationale: Somalia's case rests on self-determination for Somalis, rejecting treaties made without consulting them.

force-without-un.rationale: Officially peaceful, but Somalia fought Ethiopia in 1964 and 1977 and backed insurgents without UN approval; split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Islam is the state religion and main source of law, so faith is not subordinated to reason.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; the nation includes Somalis abroad, complicating citizenship-based lines.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The constitution promises social assistance by law but no source sets work conditions for it.

class-collaboration.rationale: A cross-class national cause stresses unity of all Somalis over class division; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The cause stresses heritage and culture, including the Dervish resistance, so sacrificing it is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: Somalia sought outside patrons, first Western and later Soviet, and was not consistently anti-Western.

workers-nation.rationale: The cause is national, not class-based, so workers would be seen as part of the nation rather than an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: A traditional Muslim society with Islamic personal status law; the constitution also gives equal rights, so a mild lean.

ban-interest.rationale: Islamic law bars riba but the 1960s state did not ban it; adherents split.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The constitution forbids discrimination by race and gives equal rights, and the cause is itself an anti-colonial one.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Shallow Marxism in Somalia; the cause sees the state as national, not class, instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Somalia produced no oil at the time and the cause says nothing about domestic fossil fuel production.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; the nation is ethnic, with citizenship given to ethnic Somalis regardless of residence.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory not found in sources; Somalia was an emigration country.

proportional-representation.rationale: The constitution provided assembly election by law; the 1960s system was proportional, but the cause has no doctrine on it.

national-mission.rationale: The cause seeks Somali unity, not spreading a governmental form; the constitution urges solidarity, not export.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed; a traditional society would resist this framing.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Barre and later critics blamed civilian politicians; clan politics under the Barre regime also drew criticism; mild lean.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Islamic framework and equal dignity under the constitution reject eugenic policy.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed by the cause; the Barre regime was later criticised for abuses.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The constitution commits the state to public health, welfare institutions and social security, beyond minimal functions.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Somali identity is based on language and descent, not race, with intermarriage with Arabs and others common; no source supports this.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The constitution gives equal rights and duties to all citizens and equal social dignity, though Islamic law sets differences by religion and sex.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not part of the cause; Barre's socialism was nationalist.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Somalis see Ethiopian and European rule over their lands as colonial, which loosely fits; the statement is about settlement.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The constitution gives Muslims personal status under sharia, and customs of others, rather than a uniform civil code.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The 1963 amendment forbids spreading any religion other than Islam.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Somalis are pastoralists whose livelihood is livestock, so a ban is unthinkable.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The constitution makes Islam teaching compulsory for Muslim pupils in primary schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not a pan-Somali doctrine; Barre's state grew stronger amid claimed encirclement, but this is a later strand.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The constitution rests on popular sovereignty and the cause rests on self-determination of Somalis.

trade-surplus.rationale: Somalia ran trade deficits financed by aid, and no source states a mercantilist aim in the cause.

population-transfer.rationale: The cause demands that Somalis remain on their land, not be expelled; no source supports pressuring minorities out.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Official formula is peaceful means and war is repudiated, but practice included force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Not addressed; clan rivalry was both a source of division and a cultural fact.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The constitution allows parties but not addressed otherwise.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed formally; anti-colonial resistance to domination by others is a theme.

separated-powers.rationale: The 1960 constitution gave legislative power to the National Assembly, with separate executive and judicial bodies.

vanguard-party.rationale: Not part of the nationalist cause; Barre's single party was a later and shallow adoption.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The constitution's labour and social protection suggest concern, but no explicit priority.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law was not a pan-Somali issue; unions were marginal in a pastoral economy.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; the cause blames partition and colonial rule.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The cause aims for one ethnically Somali state, implying that shared identity sustains unity; the claim is inferred, not stated.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The constitution provides election to the assembly and presidency.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The constitution allowed limits in emergencies; the cause itself was silent.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The cause has no stated price policy, and pastoral and market trade in food was largely informal.

party-controls-media.rationale: Independence-era constitution had free expression, though the Barre state controlled media; split by period.

party-commands-army.rationale: The constitution has the state command the army, not a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The constitution made all ethnic Somalis citizens regardless of residence, running against long waits for kin.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: No source on parliamentary pay in the cause; the 1960 constitution only provides emoluments by law.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed; Somali politics was clan-based and fluid.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Constitution accepts sovereignty limits for peace, and solidarity with African peoples, but the movement is nationalist.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The cause is silent on who commands the forces, and the constitution places the president as head of state within a parliamentary system.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Sunni Islam has no bishops and the cause has no church structure.

clerical-rule.rationale: The republic was a parliamentary democracy with Islam as state religion, not rule by scholars.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Somali nationalism supports defending the nation in conflict; no source for defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Islamic framework, inferred; oral poetry was highly valued, which tempers it.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The constitution has the Assembly elect the president, so the question of re-election was not a pan-Somali matter; no stated view.

recall-officials.rationale: The constitution sets fixed terms and Assembly dissolution but the cause has no stated view on recall.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Somalia sought alliances with patrons while claiming non-alignment; split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Property rights are guaranteed, and no Somali nationalist proposes this.

people-in-arms.rationale: Clans were armed and the WSLF fought with irregulars, but the state also built a professional army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Pastoral nomadic life is a core part of Somali cultural identity, though the claim is not stated as such.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The central aim: reuniting Somalis divided among Somalia, Ethiopia, Kenya and Djibouti by colonial borders.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: No source records pan-Somalists distrusting the educated; the SYL itself was led by educated nationalists.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed; Islamic solidarity gives a mild higher view of Islamic civilization, but no stated hierarchy.

death-penalty.rationale: Islamic criminal law and the later state used capital punishment; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: A conservative Islamic framework would resist; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; Islamic teaching compulsory for Muslim pupils but evolution not discussed.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Islamic framework as main source of law supports restriction, inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The 1961 constitution gave citizenship to all ethnic Somalis wherever they live, a descent-based rule.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; the cause demands recognition for Somali language in neighbouring states, but the statement is general.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Constitution protects freedom of conscience but restricts proselytising; exemptions not addressed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; clan and Islamic custom favour conformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; a poor aid-dependent state would favour it, inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; the 1961 constitution was drafted by a commission and no source states a view on elected assemblies.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Barre's regime did this but not the cause itself; split.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Somalia depended on aid and the constitution endorses solidarity among peoples; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Somalia had no nuclear programme and the cause never raised nuclear weapons.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The 1960 constitution has the National Assembly elect the president by secret ballot, so adherents accept parliamentary election.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Somalia's central bank was a new institution and the cause took no position on its independence.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Somali governments refused to accept the colonial treaties, such as those over the Haud, and rejected border settlements that left Somalis outside the state.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The constitution allows expropriation for public interest, and Islamic ethics condition ownership; mild lean.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed by the cause; Somalia later relied on the Soviet Union.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is outside the concerns of the cause and the 1960 constitution, so no stance is inferable.

collective-defense.rationale: Constitution favours solidarity among peoples and Somalia sought defence partners; Ethiopia and Kenya formed a defense pact against it.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Adherents hold the Ogaden, Haud and NFD were taken without Somali consent and are under foreign rule, rejecting the treaties.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Islam is the state religion, and the cause has no church-state conflict; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The president under the constitution is a head of state above the government; mild lean inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Adherents back secession for Somalis in other states but oppose their own state's breakup, as later Somaliland shows; split.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; the claim is for full union rather than autonomy inside a larger state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Sovereignty belongs to the people under the constitution, and Sunni Islam does not hold rulers divine.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The constitution says taxes are paid under law, but nothing on rate structure appears in the cause.

character-from-environment.rationale: A philosophical question not covered by sources on the cause, which defines nationhood by descent and culture rather than psychology.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The constitution subjects all state power to law and the people.

space-expansion.rationale: Entirely outside the concerns of a territorial cause in the Horn of Africa.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed; the republic was a parliamentary republic.

leader-cult.rationale: Barre fostered a personality cult as Victorious Leader, but the independence-era cause did not; split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law was governed by Islamic personal status rules, and the cause did not address shared-parenting presumptions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Barre's regime did not take this view; inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; pastoral clans held land communally.

refugee-return.rationale: Ogaden refugees from the 1977 war are a central issue and adherents would support their return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The cause rests on claiming territory because ethnic Somalis live there, though officially framed as self-determination.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Islam is the state religion with sharia as main source of law; inferred from the framework.

women-must-cover.rationale: Somali women traditionally cover the head but full covering was not legislated; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: The cause envisaged one Somali state with one currency, but no source takes a view on multinational currency unions.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The cause is defined by uniting kin Somali peoples across borders into one state.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The cause demands a state of its own for the nation, not a cultural autonomy inside Ethiopia or Kenya.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Somali nationalists reject staying as minorities in other states, demanding union with Somalia.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxism was shallow in Somalia; the cause emphasises kinship and nation.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy was not part of the cause and the economy had no industrial cartels to speak of.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not a pan-Somali concern; the state had no major banks or firms to rescue in the independence period.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; the constitution allows courts to review law.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: A conservative society with few women in politics; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Somalia relied on foreign aid and exports; the cause has no autarky aim.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The cause has no position on binding standards in trade agreements, and Somalia was a minor exporter.

moral-incentives.rationale: Barre promoted self-reliance and sacrifice but the cause did not; split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Somalia backed the WSLF and shifta guerrillas to force the issue, though the formal policy stayed peaceful.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The constitution gives equal rights and Somali clans had no formal aristocracy; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Somali nationalism teaches a shared history of Somali resistance and unity across partitioned lands.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The cause is anti-colonial and treats European and Ethiopian rule as illegitimate.

patriotic-education.rationale: The constitution sets a flag with a five-point star symbolising the claimed territories, and nationalists taught loyalty to it.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action policy is not addressed by the cause, which targets colonial partition not preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform was not part of the cause and Somalia used a conventional central-bank currency.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The cause is nationalist rather than Marxist, so it takes no side on capitalist crisis theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not applicable; Somalia had no empire, though it sought to influence former Italian and British Somali lands.

delink-world-market.rationale: Aid-dependent Somalia sought integration with partners; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The constitution forbids discrimination and clan custom stresses collective obligations.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1960 constitution has a rights section and a procedure for amendment.

decide-locally.rationale: The constitution calls for decentralised administration where possible, but the cause aims at a single unitary Somali state, so adherents split.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The cause sought political union and borders redrawn, not property reform; no source ties independence to economic transformation.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Somali governments rejected the Anglo-Ethiopian treaties over the Haud and Ogaden as made without Somali consent and in violation of self-determination.

elective-rulers.rationale: The 1960 constitution makes a president elected by the National Assembly the head of state in a parliamentary republic.

minority-veto.rationale: The constitution is parliamentary and majoritarian, so a single-member veto is inferred as rejected.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The constitution's Islamic and rule-of-law provisions imply limits on rulers, but resistance rights are inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The 1960 constitution places lawmaking in the National Assembly, not a hereditary ruler.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Islamic teaching on kindness to animals is generally upheld in the constitutional state, but this is inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The pastoral economy depends on livestock and Islamic slaughter rules; humane limits are inferred from Islamic ethics.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The constitution's welfare provisions and Islamic zakat tradition imply duties toward the poor; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: A movement aimed at uniting the nation expects citizens to take part in national politics; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Pan-Somalism took no economic doctrine; the Barre period leaned on dependency-style claims, so adherents split by period.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents are inferred as neutral.

party-own-road.rationale: Barre's Somalia allied with the USSR and later the US, and the question was not central to pan-Somalism; inferred as neutral.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Somalia relied heavily on foreign aid and the movement took no stand on it, so adherents are split.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Recovering Ogaden and the Northern Frontier District from Ethiopia and Kenya was the core aim, though they were partitioned by treaties rather than lost in war.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The movement's Somali population is largely homogeneous, so the question is mostly irrelevant; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic for the movement; nothing is stated.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The Islamic and conservative family provisions of the constitution suggest no equal-services claim; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The constitution makes Islam the state religion and builds in Islamic principles, so own-civilisation institutions are favoured; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The independence-era state built a large army yet remained parliamentary, so adherents are inferred as split.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed directly; Islam is the state religion and main source of law and Somali society is family and clan centred, so filial duty is inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: The 1960 constitution set up an elected parliamentary government; selection of rulers by examination is inferred as outside the strand.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not addressed; a nationalism focused on sovereignty and unity suggests protection of key assets from foreign buyers, inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Islamic family law is the main source of law; adherents are mixed on divorce, but a free no-fault right for either spouse is inferred as disagreed with.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The constitution sets a fixed-term parliamentary system with free mandate; binding and instant recall is not documented.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; the constitution has welfare and public-health provisions, so inferred preference for state-backed rather than private-account pensions.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The 1960 constitution protects private property; communal land-use tenure was a later Barre-era turn outside the core, so inferred disagreement.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The 1960 constitution set up an elected National Assembly with legislative and fiscal powers in a parliamentary system, consistent with approval of budgets.

single-official-language.rationale: The Somali language is the shared marker of the nation to be unified, so making it the common language is inferred, but the independence-era administration used Italian and English.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; sovereignty-minded nationalism suggests land stays with citizens, inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement is organised around ethnic-national unity, not outcome-based discrimination, inferred disagreement.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not addressed; Islamic moral teaching on moderation and ostentation is the basis of this inferred mild agreement.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Somali governments denied training guerrillas but the Shifta War in Kenya was fought by Somali kin with support broadcast and arms alleged from Somalia, and the Ogaden War followed.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Self-determination and anti-partition framing, not bloc leadership, defined the idea; forcible intervention against an ally is inferred as disagreed with.

corporate-influence.rationale: Independence-era pan-Somalism had no doctrine on lobbying or corporate power in an overwhelmingly pastoral economy with few corporations.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: A nationalism built on sovereignty and self-determination would plausibly accept limits on foreign-funded outside influence, though this is inferred, not documented.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: No documented population policy; large families were the norm and the movement's concern was reuniting Somalis, not birth rates.

residents-only-property.rationale: Land was largely communal and clan-held; the constitution protects property but no residents-only doctrine is documented.

job-guarantee.rationale: The constitution promotes work and welfare but nothing in pan-Somalism suggests a state job guarantee; inferred as indifferent.

democratic-peace.rationale: Pan-Somalism did not address democratic peace; the 1960 republic was parliamentary, but its irredentist claims on neighbours sat awkwardly with the idea.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The 1960 constitution makes obedience to law and Islam as source of law a civic order, and Somali nationalists were state-builders; inferred disagreement with a right to disregard law.

non-intervention.rationale: The movement openly claimed territory in Ethiopia and Kenya and backed armed kin there, which contradicts a rule of strict non-intervention in other states.

industrial-unions.rationale: No documented stance on union structure; the Somali Youth League and the republic were not organised around industrial labour.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Pan-Somalism blamed European and Ethiopian partition, not a hidden minority conspiracy; no such claim is documented in the sources.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The constitution makes Islam the state religion and main source of law, and Islamic family law treats marriage as a legal institution.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The constitution has rights provisions, but no stance on a right of access to government information is documented.

local-production.rationale: Pastoral and agrarian local subsistence was the norm, but no local-production doctrine belongs to pan-Somalism; inferred as indifferent.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement worked through a parliamentary state, a political party (SYL) and an army, not informal small groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The 1960 constitution has Somali law and Islam supreme at home and a nationalism centred on sovereignty; inferred preference for national over international law.

religious-nation.rationale: Islam is the state religion and Somali identity is tied to Muslim faith in the constitution, though the nation is also defined by ethnicity, language and descent.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The cause demands recognition of Somali sovereignty and equality among states; ritual tribute to a leading power is not part of it (inferred from its self-determination framing).

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: the cause seeks one unified state with national institutions, so regions retaining their own revenue cuts against pooling.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The 1960 constitution protects property but allows expropriation for public interest; no doctrine on common ownership of production is documented.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred: a Muslim-majority nationalism of the independence era with a nationalist, not Marxist, outlook; hostility to communism is not a documented tenet, and Barre-era socialism is excluded from the core.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: the 1960 constitution has a mixed economy with state welfare duties and private enterprise, but no stance on provider mix is documented.

religion-illusion.rationale: Islam is the state religion and main source of law in the 1960 constitution, so adherents would reject the view that religion is a mere illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The cause is nationalist and takes no distinctive stance on historical judgments of capitalism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed; the cause is ethnic-national and gives no distinctive position on gender and economics.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred: family and clan structures were central and the constitution gives only limited welfare duties, so public domestic services are unlikely.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; Somali script and language standardisation were debated but no purge of loanwords is documented.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed directly; the cause stresses consent in treaties dividing the Somali people, but has no documented view on treaties with internal nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: the cause aims at a unified nation-state, and the Barre-era collectivisation attempts are excluded from the core.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the cause seeks reunification of an existing people, not settlement of a majority group in minority regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Mixed constitutional economy with no stance on a third way as such; the nationalism is indifferent to the capitalism-communism axis.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Pan-Somalism rests on the claim that the Somali nation is entitled to its inhabited lands in Ogaden, the NFD and Djibouti because of shared ancestry and culture.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that a mainstream Muslim nationalism of the period would reject it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the 1960 constitution's Islamic basis; not a stated plank of pan-Somalism.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The independence-era form was parliamentary and pluralist, pursuing unification by legal means.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred from the constitution's recognition of Islam as the state religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Pan-Somalism arose as a reaction to European and Ethiopian partition and colonial rule.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred from the movement's Muslim identity and its resistance to Ethiopian rule over Somali lands; not a stated doctrine.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The independence-era mainstream was parliamentary; inferred as not endorsing removal of rulers on religious grounds.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The movement was indifferent to this question; it concerned borders and nation rather than direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its nationalist focus and Islamic social conservatism.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Islamic basis of the constitution.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Islamic norms in the constitution.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Nationalism cross-cuts left and right; the movement took no distinctive stance on the economy.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxian concept not part of the movement; Marxism entered only with Barre's later socialism, which the scope excludes.

islam-incompatible.rationale: A Muslim-majority nationalism whose constitution rests on Islam would reject this claim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred from the constitution placing sovereignty in the Somali people alongside Islam as state religion.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Islamic basis of Somali public life.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is indifferent to this labour-law question.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred from the constitution's welfare provisions and the movement's lack of a distinct economic stance.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Pan-Somalism built a large army and backed armed kin to press its claims.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the movement's unifying national aim, which favours shared rather than staged development.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from the independence-era non-aligned posture; the later Cold War alignment of the Barre era is outside the scope.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The independence-era state was a parliamentary republic founded on popular sovereignty, which excludes hereditary succession.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Islam is the main source of law, which points toward interest-free finance, but pan-Somalism has no banking doctrine; left neutral.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Its anti-colonial self-determination stance suggests resentment of outside conditions, but this is inferred and the movement did not take up the issue.

property-franchise.rationale: The constitution rests on popular sovereignty and equal citizenship, so a property bar is inferred to be unwelcome.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The idea was not addressed by pan-Somali nationalism.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept the independence-era movement did not address; Barre's shallow Marxism is excluded from the core.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Press ownership was not a pan-Somali concern, and the constitution only guarantees formal freedoms.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The 1960 constitution set up parliamentary government with rights and an independent judiciary, implying rule through public law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Pan-Somalism is ethnic in its territorial aim and in citizenship for ethnic Somalis abroad, but it did not limit the vote at home to one group; mild disagreement inferred.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic for the independence-era strand; no position can be inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Islam is the state religion and main source of law, and Islamic law restricts marriage across faiths; inferred mild agreement.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Pan-Somalism is unified around Islam and clan-ethnicity, not a boycott of a minority; inferred mild disagreement.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The movement was about territorial union, not decision-making mechanisms; nothing in its sources supports a stance.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The 1960 constitution gave Islam a foundational place, and independence-era nationalism leaned on established Sunni practice; inferred, not stated.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Pan-Somalism takes no distinctive stance on the economy or on wealth.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: A Muslim-majority nationalism with conservative Islamic social norms would oppose open gay military service, inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The 1960 constitution makes Islam the state religion and the movement is Muslim-based, so state promotion of atheism is strongly rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The movement built a large army and strong state security; abolition is not part of it, inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The independence-era state was a unitary parliamentary republic; consociational power-sharing was not a theme of pan-Somalism.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Clan and community support and Islamic charity were the traditional welfare channels in Somali society; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits were not a theme of the independence-era parliamentary movement.

vote-delegation.rationale: Standard parliamentary representation was the model; delegable votes are alien to it, inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: A modern issue the movement never addressed; inferred neutral.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Conservative Islamic norms in the movement's setting do not admit women to equal religious office, inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Conservative Islamic family norms give the husband authority, though the 1960 constitution guaranteed equality before the law; inferred at low confidence.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Citizenship and the franchise were framed around the Somali nation, so non-Somali residents voting is inferred as unwelcome; the sources do not discuss it.

rent-control.rationale: The constitution protects private property within Islamic and welfare provisions and the movement had no distinctive housing policy, so adherents are not clearly for or against rent caps.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the constitution's protection of property and a state-centred nationalism with no known stance on intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Pan-Somalism worked through parliamentary politics and a regular army; drilled national-service youth movements are not part of the mainstream independence-era form, inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from an independence-era nationalism that sought national sovereignty and peace; no nuclear question was addressed.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Pan-Somalism grew out of resisting European and Ethiopian control of Somali land, so hosting foreign bases is inferred as contrary to its sovereignty aim.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from a nationalism built on grievance over partition and the violence suffered by Somalis; the sources do not address genocide recognition directly.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the constitution's Islamic and welfare provisions, which stress work and the duty of the state to the needy.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Islamic law, on which the constitution rests, permits defence of life, and the movement backed armed kin, so absolute pacifism is inferred as rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Pan-Somalism rests on the claim that Somalis share one ethnic origin, language, religion and culture across the colonial borders.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the constitution's Islamic basis; the sources do not discuss gender theory.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the movement's conservative Muslim social outlook; not discussed in the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the cult of the anti-colonial fighters and kin who died for unification; the sources do not name martyrs explicitly.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Pan-Somalism was a secular-national, ethnic project with Islam as shared heritage, so a good-versus-evil spiritual framing is inferred as not central.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Pan-Somalism aims to gather all Somalis in a single state, the opposite of a homeland serving as a centre for a dispersed diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Its central aim was political unification into one state, so statehood is inferred as the priority over cultural renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from the traditional Islamic framing of the constitution; not discussed in the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the constitution's Islamic basis, which treats scripture as authoritative; not discussed in the sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Somalis are an overwhelming majority in Somalia and the movement had no distinctive stance on the economy, so adherents are not clearly split either way.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The core aim is to merge the Somali-inhabited Ogaden, Northern Frontier District and Djibouti with Somalia into one territorial state.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Its parliamentary, popular-sovereignty form and excluded Barre socialism imply it does not take workers' power as a test; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The constitution's welfare and public health provisions imply public provision; inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed by pan-Somalism; adherents have no distinct view.

municipal-property.rationale: The constitution protects private property and has no community-ownership programme; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The goal is union in one Somali state, not a confederation of local assemblies; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: The constitution requires equal pay but sets no family wage; no doctrine.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The ideology never addressed this question, so it is left neutral at low confidence with no basis for an inference.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The ideology never addressed this question, so it is left neutral at low confidence with no basis for an inference.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The ideology never addressed this question, so it is left neutral at low confidence with no basis for an inference.

online-anonymity.rationale: The ideology never addressed this question, so it is left neutral at low confidence with no basis for an inference.

person-over-state.rationale: The constitution's rights provisions imply the individual is not a mere means; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The constitution makes Islam the state religion and main source of law, which treats humans as having a spiritual nature.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The unitary state it seeks implies regional powers are the state's to grant; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: The ideology never addressed this question, so it is left neutral at low confidence with no basis for an inference.

dense-cities.rationale: The ideology never addressed this question, so it is left neutral at low confidence with no basis for an inference.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Pan-Somalism is an ethnic nationalism holding the Somali people have a common interest in reunification; ethnic not racial, but it maps closest.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in Somali identity and the five-pointed star flag symbolise it; inferred for ancestry-pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Officially unification was pursued peacefully but armed kin were backed and a large army built, so force was not confined to defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Pan-Somalism rests on the claim that the Somali people, united by language and culture, form one nation despite partition among several states.

communal-electorates.rationale: The 1960 republic used common electorates among Somalis, who share one religion; separate religious electorates were not an issue, so mild disagreement is inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Pan-Somalism holds that colonial powers and Ethiopia split the Somali people, and its adherents viewed neighbouring states and their backers as working to keep them divided.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the constitution's welfare and education provisions and the later Barre-era state education drive; not stated as a tuition position.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation is not addressed by pan-Somalism; no inference can be drawn from the sources.

future-generations.rationale: The ideology has no ecological doctrine; adherents are neither committed to nor against such a duty.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from the constitution's Islamic framing and equal-rights wording; no doctrine gives women's values special weight.

arms-reduction.rationale: Pan-Somalism's unification aim was backed by a large army built with Soviet aid, so reduction of arms ran against its practice.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Pan-Somali governments conducted both public claims and covert support for kin; no doctrine on diplomatic openness exists.

capital-controls.rationale: Pan-Somalism takes no distinctive economic stance; Barre-era state control and earlier open policies leave adherents split.

missingStatements.text: Colonial-era treaties that divided a people without consulting it have no binding force today.
missingStatements.rationale: Somali governments rejected the Anglo-Ethiopian treaties over the Haud and Ogaden as made without Somali consent and in violation of self-determination.

missingStatements.text: A country's constitution should commit it to seeking, by peaceful and legal means, the union of its kin people living under other states.
missingStatements.rationale: Article 6(4) of the 1960 constitution commits the Republic to promote by legal and peaceful means the union of Somali territories.

notes: The cause has no economic doctrine, so about half the answers are low-confidence 0 or inferred. The official legal-peaceful formula coexisted with force in 1964 and 1977; the profile answers force-related items as split. Barre-era scientific socialism and one-party rule would answer differently on economic and authority items.
